Management Plan

- Immediate advice to take oral antihistamine available at home.  
- Strong recommendation to call emergency ambulance rather than self-transport due to risk of rapid progression to anaphylaxis.  
- Education provided on seriousness of symptoms and need for hospital assessment and potential anaphylaxis treatment.  
- Wife instructed to remain with patient and coordinate ambulance call.  
- No further medications prescribed; no further tests ordered in primary care setting due to urgency.  
- Follow-up: Not set at this time; advised to seek emergency care immediately.

Consider:
• Record allergy to wasp venom once confirmed.  
• Arrange follow-up appointment post-hospital discharge to review reaction history, consider referral to allergy specialist, and discuss EpiPen prescription if appropriate.  
• Update immunisation status and preventive health screening at next review.
